_comment: Spawn template for a REMOTE daemon over SSH. Merge the templates block into ~/.omp/orchestrator/config.json (or point OMP_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG at this file after editing). ENROLL: 1) edit BOTH '<host>' occurrences below to your ssh target (e.g. 'user@box.example.com'); 2) install ompd on that host so 'ompd' is on the ssh PATH; 3) make sure your ssh key is authorized there (ssh-copy-id). Then `omp-orchestrator spawn <path> --template ssh-remote`. SECURITY — dial-in only: the orchestrator dials INTO the remote daemon; the daemon never dials out and never learns the orchestrator's address or state. The bearer token is minted per spawn by the supervisor, rides the ssh command line, and gates ONLY this daemon (--host 0.0.0.0 is a startup hard error without it, so a tokenless bind cannot happen). The remote sandbox holds no other daemon's token and no orchestrator credentials. The token appears in the remote process list briefly — acceptable for single-operator v1 (README Phase 6 documents the fd/stdin handoff as a follow-up); sshd config, not ompd, controls who may run the command. NOTES: the remote session file (--resume {resume}) lives on the REMOTE host under the remote cwd; use a fixed port 4721 (change it in the command if taken) — the orchestrator derives the endpoint from the template 'host' + the daemon's listening port. STOP CAVEAT: stop() kills the local ssh client; the remote daemon may survive sshd's session teardown because Bun ignores SIGHUP (verified on Bun 1.3.14) — it will idle-exit per --idle-timeout (default 30m), or add a remote-side lifecycle (systemd unit / timeout wrapper) for immediate cleanup.
